segment.description: Duck River mainstem from Shelbyville (Bedford County) downstream to Columbia (Maury County), through Bedford, Marshall and Maury counties. Warmwater black-bass/rock-bass/catfish river; this reach lies entirely BELOW the Normandy-tailwater trout water, which TWRA bounds at Three Forks Bridge, upstream of Shelbyville.
segment.boundaries: State Highway 41A bridge at Shelbyville down to Columbia; bracketed by USGS 03598000 'Duck River near Shelbyville' (Bedford Co., 35.4804/-86.4992, HUC 06040002) and USGS 03599500 'Duck River at Columbia' (Maury Co., 35.6181/-87.0323, HUC 06040003). The duck-river-tailwater catalog entry (dam to Three Forks Bridge area) is upstream and is a separate water.

damTailwater.note: The nearest cold release is Normandy Dam (TVA) far upstream, but its trout-stocked tailwater ends at Three Forks Bridge, above Shelbyville (TWRA Duck River page), so no dam tailwater applies to this reach. TWRA states even that upstream tailwater 'usually warm[s] above the 70 F mark' in non-stocking months, 'exceeding the upper limit for trout survival' - this reach is downstream of and warmer than that reach.

springFed.note: TWRA describes the Shelbyville-to-Columbia river as a warmwater bass/rock-bass/catfish float river; no spring influence is documented anywhere consulted.

coldSource.notes: Reach-specific USGS/TDEC grab record documents classic warmwater temps: summer highs of 25-28 deg C at Shelbyville and 28-32 deg C at Columbia.

holdover.detail: No holdover documentation exists for this reach and none is expected: TWRA stocks no trout anywhere on this reach (workbook has zero rows from Shelbyville to Columbia), and TWRA's own biologist text - written for the cooler tailwater immediately upstream - says river water temperatures 'usually warm above the 70 F mark' outside the Nov-Jun stocking season, 'exceeding the upper limit for trout survival'.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout presence documented in this reach; TWRA documents smallmouth/spotted bass, rock bass and catfish as the fishery. Winter put-and-take programs in the same counties (Big Rock Greenway, Marshall Co.; McCutcheon Creek, Maury Co.) are separate tributary/greenway waters, not the Duck mainstem.

troutSpecies.note: TWRA's page lists Rainbow Trout among the Duck River's fisheries, but every documented trout element on the page (Nov-Jun rainbow stocking dam-to-Three-Forks-Bridge, 7-trout creel) belongs to the tailwater reach ABOVE Shelbyville - a different catalog entry. No trout stocking or trout fishery is documented within Shelbyville-to-Columbia.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: Reach-specific USGS/TDEC grab records show 25-28 deg C summer water at Shelbyville and 28-32 deg C at Columbia, and TWRA stocks no trout here while stating even the cooler tailwater above Shelbyville exceeds the trout-survival limit outside the Nov-Jun stocking window.
